newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Littlewoods jobs to go after M&S deal.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Littlewoods jobs to go after M&S deal.

text.p: British retailer Marks and Spencer Plc on Thursday said it was buying 19 stores from Littlewoods in a deal which is likely to mean job cuts at the retail-to-football pools group.
M&S, Britain's biggest clothing retailer, said the 192.5 million pound ($323 million) deal would give it an extra 600,000 square feet of selling space in key town and city centres.

Marks has no stock or staff obligations under the agreement with Littlewoods, which means between 1,700 and 1,800 jobs are likely to go across the Littlewoods group, industry sources said. About 80 percent of these jobs would be part-time posts.
Retail analysts were positive about the acquisition, saying M&S had got a very attractive portfolio of sites, ans M&S shares rose by increased 5.5 pence to 592.5.
M&S unveiled the deal at its annual shareholder meeting along with first quarter trading figures which showed clothing sales up by nearly 10 percent.
Littlewoods, the privately owned retail-to-football pools group, last month abandoned plans to sell its entire chain of 135 high-street stores, saying it would instead sell off only selected sites.

The group will have 114 stores left after the M&S sale. It may sell a handfull of these, but plans to keep around 100, which will be revamped. The stores sold to M&S were a mixture of short and long leasehold and freehold.

There had been speculation in the press that Littlewoods, owned by the secretive millionaire Moores family, was about to clinch a deal for the 19 shops, and had been in talks with M&S, Boots Co Plc and Next Plc.
M&S chairman Sir Richard Greenbury told the annual meeting the deal would enhance shareholder value.
"This outstanding opportunity gives us an extra 600,000 square feet of selling space in key town and city centres, which again underlines our confidence in the future of the high street," he said.
The group expects to start fitting out the stores next February and intends to begin opening them progressively through the year.

The stores are in Bath, Belfast in Northern Ireland, Bromley, Cardiff, Carlisle, Chester, Derby, Edinburgh, Ilford, Kingston, Leeds, London, Dudley, Newcastle, Norwich, Peterborough, Shrewbury, Watford and Worcester.
Greenbury said the encouraging first quarter performance suggested the group was heading for another year of good progress.
Food sales were up 2.3 percent, adjusted for Easter, and in June and July were running 3.5 percent ahead of last year.
"With price deflation approaching 1.5 percent throughout the period the volume increase has, therefore, remained strong," he said.

On the recent UK government budget statement, Greenbury said the company was looking into the impact of the abolition of dividend tax credits on its pension fund and assessing the precise costs involved.
Greenbury said the reduction in corporation tax to 31 percent from 33 percent in the budget would improve the group's UK profits after tax by about 20 million pounds.

Analysts said the trading figures were quite good on clothing considering the wet weather in June. "What's really encouraging is that they've got a decent slug of Littlewood's stores," said one analyst.
